# The actual finite cover and common separator for the body-tied buffer

This verifies the hypotheses left conditional in Sections 7--8 of `candidate 26455afca6af9c16`. Work at one of that note's actual attained, sufficiently small-epsilon body minima, or at its attained interior-scale minimum. The conclusion is one actual separator for all normal-dependent convex physical fields, all cap-normal velocities, and, in the latter case, both logarithmic-scale directions. No free parameter directions or old parameter martingale are used.

The generic all-status cap expansion is the proved one in `candidate 4f875cf42fc6ba0a` and `candidate 1a7cfa3d1047cbae`. The signed energy envelope is `candidate d750a370b2e831ee`. The argument below verifies their geometric, compactness, and continuation premises for the NEW profile, and gives its exact branch formula.

## 1. Actual deepest marks and compact critical menus

Put f=H/M^(1/d), Q=M beta, with H=(E V^(1/d))^(1/(d+1)). The preceding note proves that f is continuous and concave on the canonical body, strictly concave in each positive fiber interior, zero at the own boundary, and differentiable at every own-interior mark with grad_x f=f a_Y. It also supplies a finite full supergradient there, including boundary bases, by the positive energy/volume support construction. All deepest marks have uniform own balls; all their buffered through-mark continuous cuts are proper; and their pure-base depth exceeds Q by at least v0/4.

The actual Q-superlevel set is convex. For a nonvertical full normal N=(a,u), its upper tail is continuous. Let c_Q(N) be its right Q-quantile. The condition on a mark w is the convex sublevel constraint

    N.w-epsilon f(w)Gamma(u)<=c_Q(N).

Intersect these and the closed pure-base Q-superlevel constraints. At integer bases the resulting points are precisely the actual depth-at-least-Q marks. Thus the deepest base set I is finite and lattice-complete in its convex hull.

There is exactly one deepest mark Y_p at each p in I. If two existed, their midpoint would also be deepest. An attained own-proper critical cap at that midpoint and strict own concavity of f would force contradictory strict inequality in the averaged quantile constraints. Attainment of such a cap is justified next; boundary deepest marks have already been excluded by the positive uniform depth bound.

The uniform pure-base gap allows the exact finite clipping/minimum-norm tilt reduction in Section 4 of `candidate 86dd5366456916a8`. Its hypotheses are a finite compatible base, bounded positive fibers, a continuous positive interior buffer, and that strict pure-base gap. All have just been verified. Normalize Gamma(u)=1. Near-active caps then have bounded representatives of their base tilts and thresholds, without changing the relevant local cap values. Their own coareas are bounded below. Consequently the active Q-quantile parameter set at each source is compact and nonempty. Other fibers may retain arbitrary supporting incidences.

The finite convex source minimization now yields at most d+1 active normals N_ij=(a_ij,u_ij) and positive rho_ij summing to one such that

    Gamma(u_ij)=1,
    sum_j rho_ij u_ij=epsilon grad_x f(Y_i),
    c_ij=N_ij.Y_i-epsilon f(Y_i),
    mu{N_ij.w>=c_ij}=Q.                                  (1)

This is the ordinary subgradient rule for the maximum of the compact affine-minus-f terms at its interior minimum, followed by Caratheodory in R^d. It uses no derivative of cap mass and no differentiability at other-fiber supporting traces.

## 2. At most k(P) groups cover every deepest fiber

Let B=conv I. For a source p choose a full supergradient (alpha,g) of f with g=grad_x f(Y_p). For its menu (1), put

    P_i(w)=sum_j rho_ij N_ij.w, h_i=sum_j rho_ij c_ij,
    psi_i(w)=P_i(w)-h_i-epsilon f(w),
    b_i=sum_j rho_ij a_ij-epsilon alpha.

The full tangent inequality gives psi_i(z,x)>=b_i.(z-p) on C. At every deepest mark, all selected Q-quantile inequalities are <=0, so psi_i(Y_z)<=0. Hence b_i.(z-p)<=0 on I and B. It vanishes on the minimal face of B containing p. On that face one therefore has

    psi_i>=0 on every full fiber,
    psi_i(Y_z)=0 at every deepest mark there.              (2)

All positively weighted individual quantile inequalities are equalities at these marks.

Choose one integer relative-interior witness in each inclusion-maximal occupied face of B. Their faces cover I. Two witnesses of the same parity would have an integer midpoint in the relative interior of the join face, contradicting maximality. Thus the number of groups is at most k(I)<=k(P). Use the menu of its witness for each group and let J_i be its finite set of assigned bases; overlaps may be retained or resolved once.

For every assigned base, the zero set of psi_i in its full fiber is exactly its unique interior deepest mark. Indeed two distinct zeros would make their interior segment zero by convexity and nonnegativity, contradicting strict own concavity of f. The same argument excludes an additional boundary zero by combining it with the interior zero. Thus the old contact sets are finite, with one interior contact for each assigned base. No source-to-target row, affine mark graph, or cap regularity was assumed.

## 3. One physically addable cone

Let Phi(u,z,x) be continuous in all variables, globally finite, and convex in (z,x) for each unit continuous normal u. It may have either sign. Define the ACTUAL bodies

    K_z(t)={x:u.x+t Phi(u,z,x)<=h_(K_z)(u) for every unit u}.  (3)

For small t>=0 these are positive compact convex bodies. Uniform affine lower bounds on the convex fields exclude remote points; on the resulting fixed bounded set the fields are uniformly bounded. Thus K_z(t) lies within O(t) of K_z and contains its sufficiently small inward homothety about an old inball center.

For q=sum lambda_l z_l and x_l in K_z_l(t), convexity of Phi and the old support inclusion give, for every u,

    u.(sum lambda_l x_l)+t Phi(u,q,sum lambda_l x_l)
       <=sum lambda_l h_(K_z_l)(u)<=h_(K_q)(u).

So the NEW families are compatible. Their canonical hull has exactly these sampled fibers and the same complete base.

At almost every old boundary point with its unique outer normal n, the inward normal speed is precisely Phi(n,z,x). The signed normal-roof proof applies: compare the old active n constraint with a constraint active at the new endpoint of the same interior radial ray; every limiting active normal equals n. The old inball bounds the radial denominator away from zero, and the O(t) displacement supplies domination. This proves the speed without a smoothness assumption. In d=1 there are just the two endpoint constraints.

Finite nonnegative sums of such fields remain in this class and realize the sums of their speeds. Both signs of normal-dependent affine fields are included. Append arbitrary finite cap-normal velocities, and, for an interior-scale minimum, epsilon(t)=epsilon exp(s t), s in R. Recompute V_z(t), E_(K_z(t)), M(t), Sigma(t), and f_H(t) from these ACTUAL bodies. There is no separate parameter path to choose or normalize. All finite collections therefore have a common actually feasible time interval.

## 4. Uniform contact expansion and exact global covering continuation

The old finite contacts have fixed own balls. The signed energy-envelope theorem applies to (3): its radial displacements are O(t), its normal speeds are bounded on the fixed compact bodies, and the relevant old and new minimizing energy parameters remain uniformly bounded near those source cores. Its uniform derivative is dot E=-C_E at fixed marks. The tied volume and covariance derivatives are ordinary signed shell formulas. Combining them gives exactly (13)--(15) of the preceding H-response note.

For a group i, set N_ij(t)=N_ij+t nu_ij and A_i(t)=sum rho_ij Gamma_t(u_ij(t)). Define its exact contact budget

    alpha_i(t)=min_(z in J_i,x in K_z(t))
       [sum_j rho_ij N_ij(t).(z,x)-h_i
                                  -epsilon(t) A_i(t) f_H,t(z,x)].  (4)

Every minimizer approaches the finite old zero set from (2). Otherwise uniform continuity of the bodies and f_H would leave a positive old gap, while testing an old interior contact gives alpha_i(t)=O(t). Near those contacts the old marks are interior to both bodies and the uniform first expansion applies. Nonnegativity of the old psi_i then gives

    alpha_i(t)=t min_a alpha'_ia+o(t),                  (5)

where alpha'_ia is the explicit tied-body coefficient (15), including the D_p/(d N V_p) term. No derivative of a chosen maximizing-mark path has been inserted.

Each selected cap retains a proper own section, so its new tail has a continuous strictly decreasing local inverse c_ij(t,q) near Q. The old own coarea lower bound supplies a common local interval despite other-fiber supporting facets. Solve the exact scalar equation

    sum_j rho_ij c_ij(t,q_i(t))=h_i+alpha_i(t).         (6)

For any point in a current assigned fiber, (4) and (6) imply that at least one individual buffered threshold is at least c_ij(t,q_i(t)). Its actual buffered cap therefore has mass at most q_i(t). This gives a genuine cover of the ENTIRE current assigned fibers. Off I the finite old strict gap persists by the all-normal continuity estimate. Thus strict improvement in all the group bounds gives actual strict improvement of the global normalized maximum.

## 5. All supporting allocations retained

For a fixed old cap j, let S_j>0 be its total proper-section coarea and m_j its full proper-section first moment. The generic all-status signed expansion applies to the actual O(t) radial path (3), finite plane motion nu_j, and threshold velocity r_j. Omitting only its favorable inside hinges gives the conservative loss

    R_j^0(v,nu_j,r_j)=B_j(v)+S_j r_j-m_j.nu_j
       -integral_(outside support)
                   [(nu_j.w-r_j)/|u_j|-v(w)]_+ dS.    (7)

Here B_j retains the FULL inside body capture. It also contains the proper cap part of the old boundary. Thus inside support has body selector 1 and section selector 0. Outside support keeps the same selector in both roles; it is not deleted.

Using -[a-v]_+=inf_(0<=t<=1)t(v-a), a branch chooses actual outside-face densities tau_j in [0,1]. Write

    T_j=S_j+integral_outside tau_j dS/|u_j|,
    b_j(v)=B_j(v)+integral_outside tau_j v dS,
    m_j^tau=m_j+integral_outside tau_j w dS/|u_j|.

The branch loss is b_j(v)+T_j r_j-m_j^tau.nu_j. All T_j are bounded between the previously proved S_min>0 and S_max. The branch choices form a weak-star compact set on finitely many compact supporting faces.

For contact a and group i put B_i^tau=sum_j rho_ij/T_j. Equalizing the branch cap losses with sum rho_ij r_j=alpha'_ia gives the linear branch functional

    ell_i,a,tau = [alpha'_ia
               +sum_j rho_ij b_j(v)/T_j
               -sum_j rho_ij (m_j^tau/T_j).nu_ij]/B_i^tau.    (8)

The true conservative group loss is the infimum of (8) over contacts and branches. For any branch the inequality R_j^0<=its branch gives the upper inequality; at the actual equalized thresholds choose the active hinge selectors (arbitrary values at zero displacement) to obtain equality. Proper coarea gives strict increase in each threshold and makes this equalization unique. Thus this is an actual compact family of linear supergradients, not a formal differentiability assertion.

## 6. One separator for the full cone

For fixed scale, the conservative normalized group improvement is ell_i-beta D. At an interior-scale minimum it is ell_i-beta D+M tau s. A direction making every group's improvement strictly positive would, by (4)--(7) and the off-I gaps, strictly decrease the actual objective. Attained minimality forbids that.

The downward hypograph of the group improvements is convex, since the ell_i are concave positively homogeneous on the actually addable cone. Separation from the open positive orthant therefore gives a normalized positive mixture of group/contact/branch supergradients. Equivalently, for a finite list of physical fields, the compact branch sets in (8) and finite-dimensional separation provide coefficients lambda_i,a,tau with total mass one such that their averaged linear improvement is nonpositive on every nonnegative combination of the list, and vanishes on the signed normal and scale coordinates. This is precisely the finite conservative-response dual proved in the generic nonregular theorem; (1)--(8) verify every one of its premises here. No closedness of the physical response image is needed.

For the entire physical test class use the finite-intersection argument on that compact coefficient space. Each test imposes a closed condition: branch integrals are weak-star continuous for its bounded boundary speed, T_j are uniformly positive, and contact coordinates are finite. Every finite collection has just been shown feasible. Include all cap-normal coordinates and, when available, both signs of s in each collection. Compactness therefore gives ONE choice valid for all physical fields simultaneously.

For clarity the coefficient reconstruction is explicit. Set

    kappa_ia=integral lambda_i,a,tau/B_i^tau,
    omega_ij=integral_(a,tau) lambda_i,a,tau
                                     rho_ij/(B_i^tau T_j).

Then sum_j omega_ij is the group weight and sum_i,j omega_ij=1. Averaging tau_j with these SAME body weights gives its effective outside selector. Its effective coarea satisfies

    omega_ij T_ij^eff =rho_ij sum_a kappa_ia.

The shared signed normal variables give the actual section-mean identity at the kappa-weighted contact barycenter, minus the covariance buffer shift. Define e_ia=kappa_ia delta_ia. The signed scale coefficient is M tau-sum e_ia, hence Delta=M tau when scale selection was used. No arbitrary source splitting or separate parameter dual is introduced.

Substituting the body coefficients of alpha'_ia from (15) into (8) gives EXACTLY the density (18) in the preceding H-response note:

    Xi=W-beta
      +sum_(ia:p_ia=z)e_ia[P_ia^(-N)/(N E_ia)+1/(d N V_z)]
      +(1/(2M))sum_i e_i sum_j rho_ij[u_ij.(X-g_z)]^2
      -(d+2)Delta/(2dM).

Therefore its Sections 7--8 are no longer conditional on an unverified H-specific cover or cone. All supporting allocations, contact multiplicities, and full ambient first moments have been retained.

## 7. Exact output and remaining obligation

The resulting positive normal-bundle surface law A is the sum of its actual cap capture, own-energy, own-volume, and covariance densities. It satisfies

    A <=_(normal-conditional convex order)
                  [beta+(d+2)Delta/(2dM)] sigma,

with equality of normal marginals and full conditional first moments. The already proved normal-preserving martingale construction therefore applies to this very separator. It is a SURFACE-to-SURFACE law, not an original-volume or discrete-source martingale. All denominator floors and source-core bounds proved in the preceding note apply uniformly, so its response has no free-parameter inverse/log-rate defect.

A numerical comparison between these actual surface capacities, the common projective cap credits, and outside-source-face costs remains necessary. The present theorem constructs the new variational interface and makes no claim that that comparison has already been proved.
